reason: Throughout this Exodus narrative (chapters 1-18), when the Hebrew people suffer greatly—whether from forced labor in Egypt, hunger, thirst, or fear during the Egyptian pursuit—the leaders Moses and Aaron do not tell them their suffering is their fault. Instead, when the people complain about suffering (e.g., lack of water at Rephidim, hunger in the wilderness), Moses either addresses their lack of faith ('Why do you test the Lord?') or the leaders/God provide solutions (manna, water from the rock). While Moses occasionally questions the people's faith in God, he does not attribute their suffering to their own wrongdoing or moral failings. The sufferings depicted are portrayed as challenges to overcome through trust in God, not as punishments caused by the people themselves.
